articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg just told the Financial Times that closed AI models are a strategic dead end
articles.excerpt: Mark Zuckerberg just told the Financial Times that closed AI models are a strategic dead end — and that Meta's future is open. The headline grabbed Hacker News (500+ points, 460+ comments). But beneat…
articles.body: Mark Zuckerberg just told the Financial Times that closed AI models are a strategic dead end — and that Meta's future is open. The headline grabbed Hacker News (500+ points, 460+ comments). But beneath the AI discourse lies a quieter truth: Meta has been running an open platform play for years with Quest. Open store. OpenXR. Sideloading. No gatekeepers. That openness is exactly why a two-person studio in India could build AmblyoPunch — a VR vision-training game for amblyopia — and ship it globally on day one. The Problem: Lazy Eye Treatment Is Stuck in the 1990s Amblyopia affects ~3% of the world. Standard care: patch the good eye for hours a day. Compliance is abysmal. Kids peel it off. Adults quit. Vision therapy clinics exist but are expensive, scarce, and boring.

articles.title: I Built a Codex Skill That Tries to Teach You, Not Just Write Code
articles.excerpt: AI coding assistants can generate code, explain errors, and help implement features. But there is something I've been thinking about: What happens when you can get code working but don't fully underst…
articles.body: AI coding assistants can generate code, explain errors, and help implement features. But there is something I've been thinking about: What happens when you can get code working but don't fully understand how it works? I wanted to explore that problem, so I built an open-source Codex skill called ONE_FOR_ALL . The goal is simple: make AI-assisted development more useful as a learning experience, not just a way to finish coding tasks faster. The problem I wanted to solve When working with an unfamiliar codebase, knowing what to change is only one part of the job. You also need to understand: Which files are responsible for the feature? How does data flow through the application? Why does this implementation belong here? What could break if we change it?

articles.title: LedgerMind AI: Turning a Small Business Owner's Voice Notes into Records They Can Trust
articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Most small business owners in Nigeria don't keep proper books. They keep notes: a message to themselves, a page…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built Most small business owners in Nigeria don't keep proper books. They keep notes: a message to themselves, a page in an exercise book, a voice memo. "Paid the plumber 40,000." "Client owes me 60,000." Those notes hold the real history of the business, but nobody can ask them questions like "how much did I take in this week?" or "who still owes me?" LedgerMind AI is a configurable business-record and intelligence platform that turns those everyday notes into structured records and honest reports. An owner types or speaks a note. A hosted Gemma model reads it and proposes a draft record. The owner reviews and confirms it. The backend then calculates every figure from the saved records.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle Built with PriorLabs-TabPFN. What I Built I know someone who runs a shop. Everything in it is done by hand: how much stock there is, which item is about to finish, which item people are asking for. With so much done by hand, mistakes happen. The item that sells and matters often is not there when customers come. Other times the shelf fills with stock nobody wants. That is the problem I picked. I do not have that shop's data, and I did not build this with them. So I used a public gift-shop export and treated it as the shop.

articles.title: How to categorise tickets so the numbers become usable
articles.excerpt: Short answer: A ticket category should answer what the customer asked about, not which department owns the question. Build one dimension at a time, keep the top level under thirty categories and requi…
articles.body: Short answer: A ticket category should answer what the customer asked about, not which department owns the question. Build one dimension at a time, keep the top level under thirty categories and require every category to lead to an action. Fields give structure and reporting, tags give flexibility and grow wild if nobody owns them. The category is set at closing, spot-checked, then used for knowledge gaps, staffing and automation. Every customer service tool has categories, and in most teams they mean nothing. The list was inherited from whoever set the system up, someone added a tag for a campaign in 2023, and 40 percent of tickets end up in "Other" in the report. Then management asks what customers are getting in touch about, and the answer is a guess.

articles.body: Apple has finally announced its long-rumored foldable: the iPhone Duo . The new phone has a 5.4-inch outer display and a 7.6-inch inner display, a “nano‑texture” finish on the inner screen, and barely any visible crease. Instead of Face ID, it uses Touch ID on the power button. It has two cameras, a main lens and a wide-angle lens. Apple completely revamped iOS 27’s controls and apps for the foldable, including putting the dock on the side of the phone. And it has a flashy opening animation when you unfold the phone. The iPhone Duo a big new bet from Apple, though one that’s a little late to the game compared to competitors like Samsung and Google. The phone isn’t cheap: it starts at $1,999 for the base 256GB model, and the prices only go up from there.

articles.body: The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did. An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA. "You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere , and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission .

articles.excerpt: The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week, but a bright moon makes much of the night less than ideal. Sometimes the sensible observing decision is knowing when to stay in bed — and when to get up earl…
articles.body: I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective. The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet , which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside.

articles.title: Scientists find 'gemstones' in atmosphere of bizarre, scorching-hot 'marshmallow' exoplanet
articles.excerpt: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope, astronomers have unravelled some of the secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot exoplanet that has the consistency of marshmallow.
articles.body: Using data from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), astronomers have unraveled some of the atmospheric secrets of a bizarre, blisteringly hot world that has the consistency of marshmallow. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , under the watchful infrared eye of the JWST , is WASP-17b, located around 1,300 light-years away. The exoplanet has a mass around 0.8 times that of Jupiter, but it is around twice as wide as the solar system's largest planet, giving it a "super-puff" consistency comparable to the Earth-based treat. WASP-17 b is so close to its parent star that it completes an orbit in under four Earth days, with this proximity also making the temperature of this " hot Jupiter " skyrocket.

articles.title: How to see the Orionid meteor shower 2026 peak this week — and when to look
articles.excerpt: The Orionids peak around Oct. 21. Here's when and where to look for the best chance of spotting meteors.
articles.body: If you love watching meteors, 2026 has given you plenty to enjoy. This summer, the annual Perseid meteor shower peaked on the day of a new moon — and a solar eclipse — so moonlight stayed out of the way. And there's more to look forward to: in December, the Geminids, the year's most prolific shower, will peak after a waxing crescent moon sets early in the evening, opening the door to excellent viewing. Right between those two headline showers, the dependable Orionids take their turn, reaching peak activity around Oct. 21-22. So, when and where can you catch the show? When and where to watch Make sure you wrap up warm for a night of Orionid hunting.

articles.excerpt: Tesla just unveiled its new Roadster with a spectacular stunt, using SpaceX thrusters to make the sleek vehicle "fly."
articles.body: Well, that was a memorable debut. Tesla unveiled its highly anticipated new Roadster last night (Oct. 16) with a spectacular stunt, using SpaceX thrusters to make the vehicle "fly." "This is not necessarily a safety-optimized car, OK?" Elon Musk , who runs both companies, said during the livestreamed reveal, which was held at SpaceX's rocket-testing facility in McGregor, Texas. "But it takes the the fun meter to 11 out of 10." Tesla's next-gen, thruster-equipped Roadster launches itself over other vehicles during an unveiling event on Oct. 15, 2026. (Image credit: Tesla) Tesla first announced the next-gen Roadster in 2017, saying at the time that it would be released in 2020 .
